require('minfi', quietly = TRUE) require('IlluminaHumanMethylation27kanno.ilmn12.hg19', quietly = TRUE) require('IlluminaHumanMethylation450kanno.ilmn12.hg19', quietly = TRUE) require('IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICanno.ilm10b4.hg19', quietly = TRUE) options(warn = -1)
#if str($input_source.input_mode) == 'external_grset' ## Skip internal preprocessing entirely: load an already-harmonised ## GenomicRatioSet, e.g. Stage 4 output of the cross-array harmonisation ## pipeline (Noob -> betaqn -> ComBat -> common-probe restriction). load('$input_source.external_grset') if (!exists('GRSet') && exists('GRSet.common')) { GRSet <- GRSet.common ## accommodate the harmonisation pipeline's naming } if (!exists('GRSet')) { stop("external_grset .rda must contain an object named 'GRSet' or 'GRSet.common'") }
## No raw MSet is available in this mode, so the intensity-based QC plot ## (which needs methylated/unmethylated channel medians) cannot be produced ## here. Quality was already assessed at each stage of the harmonisation ## pipeline (Stage 1 QC report, Stage 2/3 PCA plots) - point users there. writeLines( c("QC step skipped: input was a pre-built harmonised GenomicRatioSet (external_grset mode).", "Intensity-based QC is not meaningful for pre-normalised data.", "See the Stage 1 QC report and Stage 2/3 PCA plots from the harmonisation pipeline instead."), '$qctab' ) png('$qcpng') plot.new() title('QC skipped: external_grset mode - see harmonisation pipeline QC/PCA outputs') dev.off() #elif str($input_source.input_mode) == 'harmonised_idat' ## Cross-array (450K/EPIC) harmonisation, run inline from raw IDATs: ## Noob background correction -> betaqn cross-platform normalisation -> ## ComBat batch correction -> restriction to the 450K/EPIC common probe ## set -> straight into DMR/DMP hunting below. Equivalent to chaining ## the four standalone ewas_harmonisation Stage 1-4 tools followed by ## this tool's external_grset mode, but as a single tool run. require('wateRmelon', quietly = TRUE) require('sva', quietly = TRUE) require('IlluminaHumanMethylation450kmanifest', quietly = TRUE) require('IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICmanifest', quietly = TRUE)
## Stage 1 (Platform 1): Noob background correction + single dye-bias ## adjustment. Real intensity-based QC is available here (unlike ## external_grset mode, which has no raw MSet to compute it from). RGSet <- read.metharray(list.files(path='platform1', pattern='_Red.idat', full.names=TRUE)) MSet.noob <- preprocessNoob(RGSet, dyeMethod = 'single') qc <- getQC(MSet.noob) write.table(qc, '$qctab') png('$qcpng') plotQC(qc) dev.off() RSet <- ratioConvert(MSet.noob, what = 'both', keepCN = TRUE) GRSet <- mapToGenome(RSet)
#if $input_source.files_red_2 ## Stage 1 (Platform 2) + Combine Arrays: a second platform batch was ## supplied (mixed 450K/EPIC study). read.metharray can only parse one ## homogeneous array type per call - "Trying to parse different IDAT ## files, of different size and type" is what it raises if Platform ## 1 and 2 IDATs are mixed into a single call, so Platform 2 is ## Noob-corrected independently here and merged in via combineArrays, ## which aligns both GenomicRatioSets on their shared genomic ranges ## and cbinds the samples together. The QC report/plot above only ## covers Platform 1; Platform 2's own QC isn't reported separately. RGSet2 <- read.metharray(list.files(path='platform2', pattern='_Red.idat', full.names=TRUE)) MSet2.noob <- preprocessNoob(RGSet2, dyeMethod = 'single') RSet2 <- ratioConvert(MSet2.noob, what = 'both', keepCN = TRUE) GRSet2 <- mapToGenome(RSet2) ## combineArrays' internal colData merge hits a real bug ("unable to ## find an inherited method for function 'colData<-' for signature ## GenomicRatioSet, AsIs") when both inputs have completely empty ## colData (0 columns), which is the case here since neither GRSet ## has any pData set. Giving each a real column first avoids the ## degenerate empty-data-frame merge that triggers it. pData(GRSet)\$Platform <- 'platform1' pData(GRSet2)\$Platform <- 'platform2' GRSet <- combineArrays(GRSet, GRSet2) #end if
## Stage 2: Type I/II-aware cross-platform beta quantile normalisation. betas <- getBeta(GRSet) betas.norm <- betaqn(betas) assay(GRSet, 'Beta') <- betas.norm
## Stage 3: ComBat empirical Bayes batch correction. Uses the same ## phenotype table as DMP finding below, but read with a header this ## time for named batch/covariate column lookup (the DMP step further ## down reads it positionally instead - two different conventions on ## the same file, not a conflict). pheno_full <- read.table('$phenotype_table', header = TRUE, sep = '\t', check.names = FALSE) ## ComBat's batch/mod are read positionally from the phenotype table - ## there's no join by sample name anywhere in this pipeline - so a ## row count that doesn't match the number of samples in betas.norm ## (all Platform 1 samples, plus Platform 2's if used) crashes deep ## inside ComBat's design-matrix math with a bare "non-conformable ## arguments", which doesn't say anything about the phenotype table ## at all. Check the row count explicitly, before anything else here. if (nrow(pheno_full) != ncol(betas.norm)) { stop(sprintf("Phenotype Table has %d row(s) but there are %d sample(s) in your data (Platform 1 IDATs, plus Platform 2's if used). Phenotype Table needs exactly one row per sample, in the same order minfi loads your files (alphabetical by filename; Platform 1 samples first, then Platform 2's).", nrow(pheno_full), ncol(betas.norm))) } batch <- pheno_full[['$input_source.batch_column']] ## ComBat builds its own internal batch design matrix and fails deep ## inside model.matrix.default/contrasts<- with a cryptic "contrasts ## can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels" if the batch ## column isn't found or every sample shares the same value - check ## for both up front so the real problem (Batch Column Name param vs. ## Phenotype Table contents) is obvious instead of a stack trace ## pointing into ComBat's internals. if (is.null(batch)) { stop(sprintf("Batch Column Name '%s' was not found in the phenotype table's header (columns present: %s). Check the Batch Column Name parameter matches a column in your Phenotype Table exactly.", '$input_source.batch_column', paste(colnames(pheno_full), collapse = ', '))) } ## ComBat internally does as.factor(batch), which silently drops NA ## rather than counting it as a level - so a batch column with blank ## cells can pass a plain unique(batch) < 2 check (NA counts as a ## distinct value there) and still collapse to a single real level ## once inside ComBat, hitting the exact same contrasts<- crash one ## step later. Check for NA explicitly, before the level count. if (any(is.na(batch))) { stop(sprintf("Batch Column Name '%s' has a missing (blank) value for %d of %d samples in the phenotype table. Every sample needs a non-missing batch value for ComBat to run - fill in the blank cell(s) in that column.", '$input_source.batch_column', sum(is.na(batch)), length(batch))) } if (length(unique(batch)) < 2) { stop(sprintf("Batch Column Name '%s' has only one distinct value (%s) across all samples in the phenotype table. ComBat batch correction requires at least 2 batches/cohorts to correct between - if all your samples come from the same batch, set Batch Column Name to a column that actually varies (e.g. array/cohort/processing-date), or use the plain 'Raw .IDAT files' input mode instead, which skips ComBat entirely.", '$input_source.batch_column', unique(batch)[1])) } #if str($input_source.covariate_column) != 'none' covariate <- pheno_full[['$input_source.covariate_column']] ## Same contrasts<- failure mode as the batch column above, but here ## it comes straight from this model.matrix() call rather than from ## inside ComBat - same fixes, checked explicitly up front. if (is.null(covariate)) { stop(sprintf("Covariate Column Name '%s' was not found in the phenotype table's header (columns present: %s). Check the Covariate Column Name parameter matches a column in your Phenotype Table exactly, or set it to 'none' to correct for batch only.", '$input_source.covariate_column', paste(colnames(pheno_full), collapse = ', '))) } if (any(is.na(covariate))) { stop(sprintf("Covariate Column Name '%s' has a missing (blank) value for %d of %d samples in the phenotype table. Every sample needs a non-missing covariate value - fill in the blank cell(s), or set Covariate Column Name to 'none' to correct for batch only.", '$input_source.covariate_column', sum(is.na(covariate)), length(covariate))) } if (length(unique(covariate)) < 2) { stop(sprintf("Covariate Column Name '%s' has only one distinct value (%s) across all samples in the phenotype table. A covariate needs at least 2 distinct values to be modelled - either set Covariate Column Name to a column that actually varies, or set it to 'none' to correct for batch only.", '$input_source.covariate_column', unique(covariate)[1])) } mod <- model.matrix(~ covariate) #else mod <- model.matrix(~ 1, data = pheno_full) #end if betas.combat <- ComBat(dat = betas.norm, batch = batch, mod = mod, par.prior = TRUE) betas.combat[betas.combat < 0] <- 0.0001 ## ComBat can push values slightly outside [0,1] betas.combat[betas.combat > 1] <- 0.9999 assay(GRSet, 'Beta') <- betas.combat
## Stage 4: restrict to the 450K/EPIC shared probe set. probes450k <- getManifestInfo(IlluminaHumanMethylation450kmanifest, 'locusNames') probesEPIC <- getManifestInfo(IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICmanifest, 'locusNames') common.probes <- intersect(probes450k, probesEPIC) GRSet <- GRSet[rownames(GRSet) %in% common.probes, ] #else RGSet <- read.metharray(list.files(pattern='_Red.idat')) #load .IDAT files
MSet <- preprocessRaw(RGSet) #create objects contains CpGs signals
qc <- getQC(MSet) write.table(qc, '$qctab') #optional - provides a simple quality control matrix and plot png('$qcpng') plotQC(qc) dev.off()
RSet <- ratioConvert(MSet, what = 'both', keepCN = TRUE) #store Beta values and/or M values GRSet <- mapToGenome(RSet)
if ('$input_source.optpp' == 'na' ) { GRSet <- mapToGenome(RSet) #mapping Ilumina methylation array data to the genome } else if ('$input_source.optpp' == 'ppfun' ) { GRSet <- preprocessFunnorm(RGSet) #optional - implements the functional normalisation algorithm } else if ('$input_source.optpp' == 'ppq' ) { GRSet <- preprocessQuantile(RGSet, fixOutliers = TRUE, removeBadSamples = TRUE, badSampleCutoff = 10.5, quantileNormalize = TRUE, stratified = TRUE, mergeManifest = FALSE, sex = NULL) #optional - implements stratified quantile normalisation preprocessing } else if ('$input_source.optpp' == 'ppsnp' ) { snps <- getSnpInfo(GRSet) #optional - retrieve the chromosome and the position of each SNP write.table(snps, '$table') GRSet <- dropLociWithSnps(GRSet, snps=c('SBE','CpG'), maf=0) #optional - drop the probes that contain either an SNP at the CpG interrogation or at the single nucleotide extensions } #end if
pheno <- read.table('$phenotype_table',skip = 1) ## Phenotype Table's 2nd column (V2) is read positionally here and ## again below for dmpFinder - no join by sample name anywhere in ## this pipeline, same as the ComBat batch/covariate columns above. ## A row count mismatch doesn't fail here (model.matrix silently ## recycles/mismatches), but produces bogus results silently or ## crashes later downstream with a message that says nothing about ## the phenotype table - check explicitly, for every input mode. if (nrow(pheno) != ncol(GRSet)) { stop(sprintf("Phenotype Table has %d row(s) but there are %d sample(s) in your data. Phenotype Table needs exactly one row per sample, in the same order minfi loads your files (alphabetical by filename; Platform 1 samples first, then Platform 2's, if used).", nrow(pheno), ncol(GRSet))) } group <- pheno\$V2 pair <- factor(pheno\$V3) #if str($phenotype) == 'categorical' ## dmpFinder's categorical branch (further down) fits a per-group ## mean and computes an F-test per probe from the residual sum of ## squares; if every sample has its own distinct Phenotype Table ## value, there's no within-group replication left, every probe's ## residual df collapses to 0, and every p-value comes out NaN. With ## zero valid p-values left, dmpFinder's internal pi0.est() takes the ## mean of an empty vector (NaN) for every lambda cutoff and hands ## smooth.spline() an all-NaN input, which is the "missing or ## infinite values in inputs are not allowed" crash a user hit - ## nothing in that message points at the phenotype table either. ## bumphunter (right below) tolerates the same degenerate design via ## limma's rank-safe lmFit, so it can succeed even when this will ## fail - check the real requirement (>=2 groups, not one row per ## group) explicitly, before either step runs. group.levels <- unique(as.character(group)) if (length(group.levels) < 2) { stop(sprintf("Phenotype Table's 2nd column has only one distinct value (%s) across all samples. With Phenotype Type set to categorical, dmpFinder needs at least 2 groups to compare - check the 2nd column of your Phenotype Table, or switch Phenotype Type to continuous if it's a numeric measurement instead.", group.levels[1])) } if (length(group.levels) >= length(group)) { stop("Phenotype Table's 2nd column has a different value for every single sample (as many groups as samples). With Phenotype Type set to categorical, dmpFinder needs replication within each group - every group having exactly one sample leaves no residual degrees of freedom, and every p-value comes out undefined. Check that the 2nd column of your Phenotype Table is a category label (e.g. case/control) shared by multiple samples, not a per-sample identifier.") } #end if
design.matrix <- model.matrix(~ group + pair)
maxGap <- as.numeric('$maxgap_size') if(is.null(GRSet\$cluster)){ cluster = NULL maxGap = maxGap } else { cluster = GRSet\$cluster maxGap = NULL }
dmrs <- bumphunter(GRSet, design = design.matrix, cluster = cluster, maxGap = maxGap, cutoff = as.numeric('$cutoff_size'), nullMethod = '$null_method', B = as.numeric('$number_of_resamples')) dmrGR <- dmrs\$table[,c(1,2,3)] colnames(dmrGR) <- c('chr','start','end') write.table(dmrGR, file= '$dmr', quote = FALSE,col.names = TRUE, row.names = FALSE, sep = '\t')
tab <- read.table('$ucsc_genome') tab <- tab[,-(11:14),drop=FALSE] tab <- tab[,c(1,4,5,10)] colnames(tab) <- c('chr','start','end','names')
dmp <- dmpFinder(dat = getBeta(GRSet),pheno = group, type = '$phenotype', qCutoff = as.numeric('$q_cutoff'), shrinkVar = '$variance_shrinkage') dmp[,'names'] <- rownames(dmp) data <- merge(dmp, tab, by='names',sort = TRUE) data <- data[,c(6,7,8,1,4,5)] ## Round pval/qval to 6 significant figures: raw double precision varies ## in the far decimal places across R/Bioconductor point releases (e.g. ## different BLAS backends), which made byte-exact test comparisons ## fail despite identical probe ordering and effectively identical values. data[,5] <- signif(data[,5], 6) data[,6] <- signif(data[,6], 6) write.table(data, file= '$dmp', quote = FALSE,col.names = TRUE, row.names = FALSE, sep = '\t')

param.name: input_mode
param.label: Input data source
param.help: Choose raw IDATs to run full in-tool preprocessing, raw IDATs with cross-array harmonisation for mixed 450K/EPIC studies, or supply an already-harmonised GenomicRatioSet to skip preprocessing entirely.
param.option: Raw .IDAT files with cross-array harmonisation (Noob + betaqn + ComBat + common-probe, for mixed 450K/EPIC studies)

param.name: files_red
param.label: Red .IDAT files
param.help: Red .IDAT files extension is followed by the unmethylated signal intensity read in the red channel.

param.name: files_grn
param.label: Green .IDAT files
param.help: Green .IDAT files extension is followed by the methylated signal intensity read in the green channel.

param.name: optpp
param.label: (Optional) Preprocessing Method
param.help: Mapping Ilumina methylation array data to the genome with or without additional preprocessing methods.

param.name: files_red
param.label: Platform 1 Red .IDAT files
param.help: Red .IDAT files extension is followed by the unmethylated signal intensity read in the red channel. All samples here must be the same array type (e.g. all 450K) - minfi can only parse one array type per batch; use the Platform 2 fields below for a second, different array type (e.g. EPIC).

param.name: files_grn
param.label: Platform 1 Green .IDAT files
param.help: Green .IDAT files extension is followed by the methylated signal intensity read in the green channel. Must match Platform 1 Red files 1:1 by sample.

param.name: files_red_2
param.label: (Optional) Platform 2 Red .IDAT files
param.help: For mixed-platform studies only (e.g. Platform 1 = 450K, Platform 2 = EPIC). Noob-corrected separately from Platform 1, then merged in via minfi::combineArrays before cross-platform normalisation. Leave empty for single-platform runs.

param.name: files_grn_2
param.label: (Optional) Platform 2 Green .IDAT files
param.help: Must match Platform 2 Red files 1:1 by sample. Leave empty for single-platform runs.

param.name: batch_column
param.label: Batch Column Name
param.help: Name of the column in the phenotype table identifying batch/cohort/array-of-origin, passed to ComBat as the batch covariate.

param.name: covariate_column
param.label: Covariate Column Name (optional)
param.help: Name of a column to preserve as a biological covariate in the ComBat model (e.g. phenotype/disease status), or "none" to correct for batch only.

param.name: external_grset
param.label: Pre-built GenomicRatioSet (.rda)
param.help: Must contain an object named GRSet or GRSet.common - e.g. the Stage 4 output of the cross-array harmonisation pipeline (Noob -> betaqn -> ComBat -> common-probe restriction).

param.name: phenotype_table
param.label: Phenotype Table
param.help: Table of compared samples and their characteristics, may be categorical (e.g. cancer vs. normal) or continuous (e.g. blood pressure). Must include the following information: sampleID, phenotype and paird or unpaired samples column.

param.name: maxgap_size
param.label: maxGap Size
param.help: If cluster is not provided this maximum location gap will be used to define cluster.

param.name: cutoff_size
param.label: Cutoff Size
param.help: A numeric value. Values of the estimate of the genomic profile above the cutoff or below the negative of the cutoff will be used as candidate regions. It is possible to give two separate values (upper and lower bounds). If one value is given, the lower bound is minus the value.

param.name: number_of_resamples
param.label: Number of Resamples
param.help: An integer denoting the number of resamples to use when computing null distributions. This defaults to 0. If permutations is supplied that defines the number of permutations/bootstraps and B is ignored.

param.name: null_method
param.label: null Method
param.help: Method used to generate null candidate regions (defaults to ‘permutation’). Note that for cases with more than one covariate the permutation approach is not generally recommended.

param.name: q_cutoff
param.label: qCutoff Size
param.help: DMPs with an FDR q-value greater than this will not be returned.

param.name: variance_shrinkage
param.label: Variance Shrinkage
param.help: Enable variance shrinkage is recommended when sample sizes are small.

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
The workflow combines 5 main steps, starting with raw intensity data loading (.idat) and then optional preprocessing and normalisation of the data. The next quality control step performs an additional sample check to remove low-quality data, which normalisation cannot detect. The workflow gives the user the opportunity to perform any of these preparation and data cleaning steps, including the highly recommended genetic variation annotation step resulting in single nucleotide polymorphism identification and removal. Finally, the dataset generated through all of these steps can be used to hunt (find) differentially-methylated positions (DMP)and regions (DMR) with respect to a phenotype covariate.
***Input data source***
*Raw .IDAT files*: standard single-array-type workflow - loads raw intensity data and runs this tool's own preprocessing (optional Funnorm/Quantile/SNP-removal below).
*Raw .IDAT files with cross-array harmonisation*: for studies mixing 450K and EPIC samples. Runs Noob background correction, wateRmelon's Type I/II-aware betaqn cross-platform normalisation, sva's ComBat empirical Bayes batch correction (batch column configurable, e.g. cohort/array-of-origin), and restriction to the 450K/EPIC shared probe set, all inline, before proceeding straight into DMR/DMP hunting below. Equivalent to chaining the four standalone ewas_harmonisation Stage 1-4 tools into this tool's external_grset mode, as a single tool run. Real intensity-based QC is reported (from the Noob step), unlike the pre-built-GenomicRatioSet mode below.
If your samples span two genuinely different array types (e.g. some run on 450K, some on EPIC), put one platform's files in the Platform 1 fields and the other's in the optional Platform 2 fields - ``minfi::read.metharray`` can only parse one homogeneous array type per call ("Trying to parse different IDAT files, of different size and type" is the error you'd otherwise see), so each platform is Noob-corrected independently and merged via ``minfi::combineArrays`` before cross-platform normalisation continues. Leave the Platform 2 fields empty for ordinary single-platform runs. The standalone ewas_harmonisation suite has an equivalent standalone **Combine Arrays** tool for the same purpose when chaining Stage 1-4 manually instead of using this inline mode.
When Platform 2 is used, the Phenotype Table must have one row per sample across *both* platforms, ordered Platform 1's samples first then Platform 2's (each block alphabetically by filename, matching how ``read.metharray`` orders columns) - the batch/covariate columns are read positionally, not joined by sample name, so a phenotype table sized for one platform only will make ComBat fail with a "non-conformable arguments" error once the two platforms are merged.
*Pre-built GenomicRatioSet*: skips preprocessing entirely - supply an already-harmonised ``GRSet``/``GRSet.common`` .rda, e.g. produced by running the standalone ewas_harmonisation Stage 1-4 tools separately first.
***Inputs***
*Series of .IDAT files*: matching red and green .idat file for each sample on the chip intensity data.
*(optional) Preprocessing Methods*: by this step probes can be stratified by region via quantile normalisation or by extended implementation of functional normalisation recommended for cases where global changes are expected such as in cancer-normal comparisons. In addition unwanted probes containing either an SNP at the CpG interrogation or at the single nucleotide extension can be removed (recommended). Only applies to the plain Raw .IDAT files mode.
*Phenotype Table*: table of compared samples and their characteristics, may be categorical (e.g. cancer vs. normal) or continuous (e.g. blood pressure).
========== ============== =============== Accession Sensitivity Treatment ---------- -------------- --------------- GSM1588704 sensitive MAPKi ---------- -------------- --------------- GSM1588705 sensitive MAPKi ---------- -------------- --------------- GSM1588706 resistant BRAFi ---------- -------------- --------------- GSM1588707 resistant BRAFi ========== ============== ===============
*Note*: phenotype covariate table must include the following information: sampleID/Accession, phenotype and paird or unpaired samples column
*Genome Table*: a reference genome that contains the nucleotide sequence of the chromosomes, It is representative of a specific genome build and release.
***Outputs***
*Quality Control Report and Plot*: quality control (QC) outputs plot of the log median intensity in both the methylated (M) and unmethylated (U) channels. When plotting these two medians against each other the good samples cluster together, while failed samples tend to separate and have lower median intensities.
*(optional) SNPInfo Table*: matrix of the chromosome and the position of each SNP on a given Affymetrix SNP Array.
*Differentially Methylated Regions*: consecutive genomic locations differentially methylated in the same direction save as multiple track lines in a single BED file.
*Differentially Methylated Positions*: single genomic position that has a different methylated level in two different groups of samples (or conditions) save as multiple track lines in a single BED file.
